# I built a Markdown editor for the Mac that does sums beside your text

Coffee 1.3 is out: plain .md files, answers to sums beside the line, and maths and diagrams drawn natively.

By Mr\_PFT

November 8, 2026

I've been building Coffee, a Markdown editor for the Mac written in Swift with AppKit and TextKit 2, and no third-party dependencies. Your notes stay plain .md files in a folder you pick, so Git, iCloud Drive or anything else can sit on top.

A few things it does that I couldn't find together elsewhere: [...] ·

results.title: My best 6 markdown editors in 2026
results.content:
Want a full knowledge base and don’t mind the climb? Obsidian.
   Want quiet, distraction-free prose? iA Writer.
   Write long-form and live in the Apple world? Ulysses.
   Want beautiful notes on your Apple devices? Bear.
   Want free, open source, and live rendering? MarkText.
   Just want to open a `.md` file and read or edit it without fuss on Mac, Windows or Linux? That’s the gap I built Markdific for. On Mac, it also adds Quick Look support, so you can preview Markdown files directly in Finder by pressing the Space bar. Obvious bias noted. [...] On Mac, Markdific adds Quick Look support, so I can preview a Markdown file in Finder by selecting it and pressing the Space bar. The preview draws Mermaid diagrams, colours code blocks and shows images stored next to the file.
   I can edit a Markdown file without remembering all the syntax because there’s a small formatting toolbar. When I blank on how to build a table, I just click the button.
   Autosave quietly does its thing in the background, so I stopped worrying about saving every few minutes.
   There’s a proper dark mode, plus Nord, Dracula and Paper themes and a font picker for changing how the document reads.
   Split view shows me the raw Markdown beside the rendered document when I need both.
   An outline sidebar saves me a lot of scrolling in long documents.
